evidence: Receiving DO2 falls from 12.25 mg/L at t=48.0 h to 6.45 mg/L at t=48.2 h and continues drifting down to 5.74 mg/L at t=52.0 h
Source DO2 at same window (48-52 h) stays ~11 mg/L; source P=3.01 g/L vs receiving P=3.64 g/L at 48 h assays
Latest delayed product assay (t=48 h, available t=52 h): P=3.64 g/L and rising
Allowed action bounds: increase_air = aeration x1.15, feed unchanged; minimum DO2 constraint = 2.0 mg/L
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 dropped abruptly at 48.2 h from ~12.3 to ~6.5 mg/L and is slowly declining (5.74 mg/L at 52 h), diverging from the source profile (~11 mg/L at the same age). Growth/productivity is strong (P=3.64 g/L at 48 h), so oxygen demand has outrun transfer capacity. A bounded aeration increase (x1.15) raises DO2 without cutting feed, retaining product mass and avoiding the 2.0 mg/L oxygen constraint. Feed reductions (reduce_feed, strong_feed_reduction) would sacrifice product mass unnecessarily; stop yields zero production; KEEP risks continued DO2 decline with no corrective margin.
args.uncertainty: The decline rate (~0.17 mg/L/h) is slow relative to the 2.0 mg/L minimum, so KEEP is defensible if the DO2 plateau reflects a new equilibrium rather than a continuing trend; only 20 h of post-drop data exist. The exact aeration headroom of the receiving vessel is unknown, so the DO2 benefit of x1.15 aeration is estimated, not measured. If DO2 keeps falling after the intervention, a combined or strong feed reduction would be the next escalation.
